propositions: On git >=2.47 with ADR 0051 config (foreground auto-maintenance), git commit runs git maintenance run --auto synchronously inside the subprocess, charging O(store) repack cost to the 30-second _GIT_TIMEOUT bound.

When a store accumulates loose objects past git's ~6700 threshold, the triggering lock-held commit is SIGKILLed mid-repack if repack duration exceeds 30 seconds, losing the write and risking mid-operation corruption.

Suppressing auto-maintenance on the bounded commit via -c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false makes the commit O(1)-fast, then deferring git maintenance run --auto as an explicit post-commit step under the same write lock preserves ADR 0051 serialization while removing the O(store) cost from the latency bound.

The failure class requires decoupling inline maintenance from the commit bound on all lock-held store-commit surfaces: event_append primary and recovery paths, txn claim/transition, delete, compact_plan, compact, and fsck_repair.
Regression test RED->GREEN confirms that under the suppressed-then-deferred maintenance pattern, a write with sufficient loose objects succeeds within the 30-second bound instead of timing out.
